thread:
Maya T: saw a recon mismatch — Stripe usage invoice totals for product 'Compute-hours' don't match NetSuite generated AR totals for Jan. Looks like rounding differences.

Billing Bot: Alert: 2026-04-02T03:14:22Z — aggregate mismatch detected for invoice_batch b_202601_jan_compute, delta: 0.13 USD.

Owen L: rounding is expected when per-line usage is prorated/sliced; however delta of $0.13 could be due to mix of currency conversions + cents truncation. Can you paste a sample invoice id?

Maya T: in_1MabC2 and in_1MabF7. Sample line items: "compute: 13.333333 hours @ $0.009 = 0.119999997" which Stripe rounds to 0.12, NetSuite line calc uses integer-cents math and ended up showing 0.11 when aggregated in that export.

Carlos R: NetSuite integration uses integer cents math; if we multiply then truncate before summing we can get off-by-one-cent differences per line that accumulate.

Priyanka M: we had a similar issue in 2025-11 and added a 'round_half_up' helper in billing-core PR #4010 but netsuite-import expects banker's rounding for audit. There's a mismatch in rounding mode.

Owen L: sounds like mismatch between billing rounding and netsuite rounding. Proposal: 1) audit a sample of invoices to quantify, 2) add reconciliation rule to tolerate <= $0.25 discrepancy automatically after accounting OK, 3) align rounding functions by applying explicit cents rounding before sending to NetSuite, 4) add an automated E2E check to export pipeline.

Maya T: please run the audit and list affected invoice ids so Accounting can review flags.

Owen L: running audit now, ETA 30m. Billing Bot: Job started: rounding-audit v2.

Maya T: also flag any multi-currency invoices. Currency-conversion rounding multiplies the effect.

Carlos R: Accounting approves tolerance up to $0.25 for usage billing (email thread archived). We still want to fix misalignment for future exports.

Priyanka M: I'll prepare a patch to netsuite-export to use billing-core's rounding helper and add a runtime feature flag NETSUITE_USE_BILLING_ROUNDING=false defaulting to false so we can toggle. Also adding unit test comparing per-line totals.

Owen L: audit results: 128 invoices with deltas from $0.01 to $0.47, median $0.09. 32 invoices > $0.20 flagged for manual review.

Maya T: thanks. We'll re-export the 32 after patch is deployed and confirm with Accounting. Filing FIN-1133 to track fixes, export migration, and any customer comms.

Carlos R: good catch. Add an integration test that runs a representative usage batch and compares Stripe total vs NetSuite exported total end-to-end.

Priyanka M: will include that in PR #5287.
